label: depth staging: shot checks against the set and foreground framing

scenarios.why: A face hidden behind a prop is a sight line from the lens to the eyes; the shot check samples it over every shot.

scenarios.request: is something in the way of his eyes?
scenarios.why: Something in the way of the eyes is the same occlusion question asked in plainer words.

scenarios.request: is the camera inside the wall?
scenarios.why: A lens inside set geometry renders the inside of the wall; the inside rule tests the lens against every prop box.

scenarios.request: is the lens poking through the door frame?
scenarios.why: A lens through a door frame sits inside or within the near clip of it, which is the inside rule.

scenarios.request: does the frame cut Mara at the knees?
scenarios.why: A frame edge on a joint reads as an amputation; the crop rule places the knee from the figure's proportions.

scenarios.request: does the bottom edge chop Joon at the ankles?
scenarios.why: Chopping at the ankles is the low crop: show the feet or lose the shins, the check says which.
Checking the shots with no rule named runs every rule against the set; checking cuts is a different question.

scenarios.request: put the lamp in the foreground
scenarios.why: A prop in the foreground is placement through the lens: the solve moves the camera so the lamp covers part of the frame.

scenarios.request: frame Mara with Joon's shoulder soft in the foreground
scenarios.why: A person's shoulder in the foreground is the over-the-shoulder solve with that person as the near layer.

scenarios.request: a sliver of the doorway in the foreground on Joon
scenarios.why: A sliver asks for a small share of the frame; the doorway is the near layer and Joon the subject.

scenarios.request: are we clipping into the bookcase?
scenarios.why: We means the camera and a bookcase is set geometry; the resolver knows neither word yet.
